i. The members of these bodies are directly elected by the people.
ii. Elections shall be held within a period of 3 months from the dissolution of the body.
iii. Women have been given 1/3 reservation in Panchayats.
iv. The minimum age required to become member is 21 years.
147.x: Members are directly elected (i), women get one-third (iii) and the minimum age is 21 (iv); ii is wrong as fresh polls must be held within six months, not three.

147.s: Election was held on 20 January, 2014 for a Gram Panchayat. Its first meeting was called on 10 February 2014. Thereafter Gram Panchayat was dissolved on 20th February, 2016. Election was held on 15th May, 2016 for New Gram Panchayat and, its first meeting was called on 25th May, 2016. What shall be tenure of the new constituted Gram Panchayat?
147.x: A Panchayat reconstituted after early dissolution serves only the remainder of the dissolved body's five years from its first meeting (10 Feb 2014) – so till 10 Feb 2019.

147.s: If a Panchayat is dissolved, elections are to be held within–
147.x: Art. 243E: on dissolution, elections must be completed within six months.

147.s: Territory of a Kshetra Panchayat (Panchayat at intermediate level) is determined by –
147.x: The intermediate level and its area are specified by the Governor (State Government) by public notification (Art. 243(c)); the SEC only conducts polls.

147.s: If the President of Zila Panchayat is suspended, what will be happened?
o: The Vice President of Zila Panchayat will act as acting President.
The Vice President will become President.
The Office of the President will be vacant.
The members will elect President temporarily.
147.x: Under the Chhattisgarh Panchayat Raj Act the members elect a President temporarily when the President is suspended (CGPSC 2017 key); the Constitution leaves this to State law.

147.s: Which one of the following statements with regard to the functioning of the Panchayats is not correct?
o: Panchayats may levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls, etc.
A person who has attained the age of 25 years will be eligible to be a member of a Panchayat.
Every Panchayat shall ordinarily continue for five years from the date of its first meeting.
A Panchayat reconstituted after premature dissolution shall continue only for the remainder of the full period.
147.x: The minimum age for Panchayat membership is 21, not 25; the other statements (taxes, five-year term, remainder after dissolution) are correct.

147.s:
Match List I (Names of the Panchayat Samitis) with List II (Provinces of India) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists.
List I
A. Janpad Panchayat
B. Kshetra Panchayat
C. Taluka Parishad
D. Anchalik Parishad
List II
1. West Bengal
2. Gujarat
3. Madhya Pradesh
4. Uttar Pradesh
Codes A B C D
147.x: Janpad Panchayat – Madhya Pradesh, Kshetra Panchayat – Uttar Pradesh, Taluka Parishad – Gujarat, Anchalik Parishad – West Bengal in the CGPSC list: code 3 4 2 1.

147.s: What is not Legal?
o: An MLA who is ex-officio member of Janpad Panchayat can nominate representative to participate in the meeting.
A member of Lok Sabha who is ex-officio member of Zila Panchayat can nominate representative to participate in the meeting.
A member of Rajay Sabha who is ex-officio member of Zila Panchayat can nominate representative to participate in the meeting.
A woman Sarpanch can nominate her husband to participate in the meeting of Gram Panchayat and Janpad Panchayat
147.x: A woman Sarpanch cannot nominate her husband to attend Panchayat meetings ('Sarpanch-pati' proxy is not legal); ex-officio MLAs and MPs may nominate representatives under the State Act.

147.s:
What is not correct about Gram Panchayat?
I. The maximum strengh is 20 panchs in a Gram Panchayat.
II. If 15 panchs are elected in Gram Panchayat, nominated.
III. The President of Janpad Panchayat nominates 5 panchs.
IV. The strength may be 10 panchs in a Gram Panchayat.
V. In case of equal votes in the election of panchs it is decided by lott.
VI. Nominated members participate in the meeting and can vote. Code
147.x: CGPSC 2015 key: II, III and VI are not correct under the Chhattisgarh Act (nominated members do not take part in voting); the composition of a Gram Panchayat is a State-law matter.

147.s:
Which of the following statements with regard to Panchayats in India are correct?
I. Seats in a Panchayat are filled by direct election from the territorial constituencies in the Panchayat area.
II. The Gram Sabha is the body of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the Panchayat area.
III. The Panchayats work on the principle of constitutional autonomy.
IV. The State Legislature may by law endow the Panchayats with the power and authority to enable them to function.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
147.x: Seats are filled by direct election (I), the Gram Sabha is the body of registered voters (II), and powers come from State law (IV); Panchayats have no 'constitutional autonomy' (III).

147.s: Who among the following is authorized to make provisions with respect to the composition of Panchayats?
147.x: Art. 243C(1): the Legislature of a State may by law provide for the composition of Panchayats.

147.s: The members of the Panchayat Samiti are –
o: Nominated by the Block Development Officer
Nominated by the Chairman of Zila Panchayat
Indirectly elected by the members of the Village
147.x: All members of Panchayats at village, intermediate (Panchayat Samiti) and district levels are directly elected by the people.

147.s:
Consider the following statements :
I. Panchayats at the intermediate level exist in all States.
II. To be eligible to be a Member of a Panchayat at the intermediate level, a person should attain the age of thirty years.
III. The Chief Minister of a State constitutes a commission to review the financial position of Panchayats at the intermediate levels and to make recommendations regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes and duties, leviable by the State, between the State and Panchayats at the intermediate level.
Which of the statements given above are not correct?
147.x: All three are wrong: the intermediate tier is optional for States up to 20 lakh, the minimum age is 21 (not 30), and the SFC is constituted by the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

147.s: Which of the following is not correct with respect to the composition of Panchayat?
o: The Legislature of a State may by law make provision
A Gram Sabha shall exercise it’s powers at the village
Each State will constitute Panchayat at the village,
Panchayat at the intermediate level shall not be
147.x: Art. 243B(2) says intermediate Panchayats 'may not' be constituted in a State of 20 lakh or less – so 'shall not be' is the incorrect statement; the rest restate 243A-243C.

147.s: The Members of Panchayat Samiti are -
o: Elected by the members of Panchayat
Recruited on the basis of open competition
147.x: Panchayat Samiti members are directly elected by the people; only intermediate and district chairpersons are elected indirectly.

147.s: Intermediate level Panchayats need not be constituted by a State with a population of
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
147.x: Under Art. 243B(2) a State with population not exceeding 20 lakh need not constitute intermediate Panchayats.

147.s: The 73rd Constitutional amendment introduced?
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
147.x: The 73rd Amendment introduced a three-tier system – village, intermediate and district.

147.s: As per the provisions of the constitution, the President of a panchayat shall be elected in the following manner?
o: Direct election by the voters of the Panchayat
Election by the Ward members of the Panchayat
As per the Law framed by State Legislature
As per the manner prescribed by the Lok Sabha
147.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
147.x: Art. 243C: the chairperson of a village Panchayat is elected in the manner the State Legislature provides by law – the Constitution fixes neither direct nor indirect election.

147.s: Panchayats at the Intermediate Level may not be constituted in a State having a population not exceeding
147.x: Art. 243B(2): a State with a population not exceeding 20 lakh may not constitute panchayats at the intermediate level.

147.s: Who assigns and authorizes the collection of certain taxes by Panchayats?
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
147.x: Under Art. 243H the State Legislature may by law authorise a Panchayat to levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls and fees; the Governor, Collector or President has no such role.

147.s: According to Constitutional Provisions the decision to hold Panchayat elections is taken by -
147.x:
Most books and keys: State Government. Strictly: Art. 243K vests superintendence, direction and control of Panchayat elections in the State Election Commission (Laxmikanth ch.39 p.104).
The book/official key is the State Government, which notifies the schedule; but under Art. 243K the conduct of all Panchayat elections is vested in the State Election Commission, which must hold them on time (Kishansing Tomar, 2006).

147.s: The decision to conduct Panchayat Elections is taken by which of the following?
147.x:
Most books and keys: State Government. Strictly: the State Election Commission (Art. 243K) controls and conducts Panchayat elections.
The keyed answer is the State Government (Panchayats are a State subject); strictly, the State Election Commission under Art. 243K conducts and controls Panchayat polls. The Central Government, District Judge and ECI have no role.

147.s:
Consider the following statements regarding State Election Commission, Rajasthan -
1. The State Election Commission, Rajasthan was constituted in December, 1994
2. It has a secretary who is also the Chief Electoral Officer for the state.
147.x: Only (ii): the Rajasthan SEC was constituted in July 1994 (Governor's order 17 June 1994, working from 1 July 1994), not December; its Secretary is also the State's Chief Electoral Officer.

147.s:
Which of the following are Constitutional Authorities?
Select the correct answer using code given below :
1. State Election Commission
2. State Finance Commission
3. District Panchayat
4. State Electoral Officer
147.x: SEC (243K), SFC (243I) and the District Panchayat (243B) are created by the Constitution; the Chief Electoral Officer of a State is a statutory officer under s.13A of the RP Act 1950.

147.s:
The Constitution (Seventy-Third Amendment) Act, 1992, which aims at promoting the Panchayati Raj Institutions in the country, provides for which of the following?
1. Constitution of District Planning Committees.
2. State Election Commissions to conduct all Panchayat elections.
3. Establishment of State Finance Commissions.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
147.x: Part IX provides State Election Commissions (243K) and State Finance Commissions (243I); District Planning Committees (243ZD) come from the 74th Amendment – so 2 and 3 only (UPSC 2011).

147.s:
Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the State Finance Commission?
I. It is required to appoint a State State Finance Finance Commission once in five years.
II. It recommends the determination of taxes, duties, tolls and fees assigned to the Panchayats and Municipalities.
III. Article 243 deals with constitution of finance commission to review financial position of 36. Panchayats.
147.x: The SFC is constituted every five years (I) and recommends the taxes, duties, tolls and fees assigned to Panchayats (II); III is wrong because the SFC Article is 243I, not 243.

147.s: For election to the Panchayat, the State Election Commissioner will be appointed by
o: The Chief Election Commissioner of India
147.x: Under Art. 243K the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and removable only like a High Court judge – not by the CEC, President, Chief Justice or Home Minister.

147.s: Under which Article the State Election Commission Operates the election of urban bodies?
147.x:
Most keys: 243K. Strictly: municipal elections are under Art. 243ZA, which uses the SEC constituted under 243K.
Art. 243K constitutes the State Election Commission; Art. 243ZA vests municipal elections in 'the State Election Commission referred to in article 243K', so 243K is the keyed answer among these.

147.s: Who recommends to the Governor the principles which should govern the distribution between the state and the panchayats of the net proceeds of the taxes and Fees leviable by the State, which may be divided between them?
147.x: The State Finance Commission (Art. 243I) recommends to the Governor the principles for sharing the net proceeds of State taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the State and the Panchayats.

147.s: The power to legislate on all matters relating to elections to Panchayats lies with
147.x: Art. 243K(4): the State Legislature may by law provide for all matters relating to Panchayat elections; the SEC conducts them and the ECI has no role.

147.s: How many times Panchayat General Election have taken palce after formation of Madhya Pradesh State Election Commission?
147.x: Since the MP SEC was formed (1 Feb 1994), Panchayat general elections were held in 1994, 1999-2000, 2004-05, 2009-10 and 2014-15 – five by 2020.

147.s:
73rd and 74th Amendments of the Constitution are responsible for the creation of which of the following?
1. State Election Commission
2. District Planning Committee
3. State Finance Commission
4. State Property Tax Valuation Board
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
147.x: The 73rd and 74th Amendments created the SEC (243K/243ZA), SFC (243I/243Y) and District Planning Committee (243ZD); there is no constitutional property-tax valuation board.

147.s: Which statement is correct about Panchyati Raj?
o: The Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad are constituted
Minimum age is 18 years to contest the election at the
Election of the Panchayati Raj Institutions is
147.x: Elections of PRIs are conducted by the State Election Commission (Art. 243K); the minimum age to contest is 21, not 18.

147.s:
Study the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below:
Assertion (A) : The State Election Commission is a Constitutional authority.
Reason (R) : Elections to rural local bodies are overseen by the Election Commission of India.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
147.x: The SEC is a constitutional authority (Art. 243K), but Panchayat polls are overseen by the SEC, not the Election Commission of India – A true, R false.

147.s: State Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by
147.x: Under Art. 243K the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and removable only like a High Court judge – not by the CEC, President, Chief Justice or Home Minister.

147.s: All elections to the Panchayats are conducted by-
147.x: Art. 243K vests the conduct of all elections to the Panchayats in the State Election Commission.

147.s: Who among the following constitutes “Finance Commission” to review the financial position of Panchayats?
o: Chief Minister of the concerned State
Finance Minister of the concerned State
The Governor of the concerned State
Panchayati Raj Minister of the concerned State
147.x: Art. 243I: the Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission within one year of the 73rd Amendment and every five years thereafter.

147.s:
Consider the following functions of State Election Commission and select the correct answer using the code given below?
1. Prepares the electoral rolls for Panchayats and Municipalities elections in the State.
2. Conducts elections for Panchayats and Municipalities of the State.
3. Conducts elections for other bodies in addition to Panchayats and Municipalities in accordance with the directions given by the Governor.
4. Prepares the electoral rolls and conducts elections as assigned by Election Commission of India.
147.x: Arts. 243K(1) and 243ZA(1) vest the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all Panchayat and Municipal elections in the SEC; other bodies and Assembly/Lok Sabha rolls are not its constitutional job.

147.s: All Panchayats elections must be conducted by the State Election Commission mentioned in Article ____ of Indian constitution
147.x: Panchayat elections are conducted by the State Election Commission under Article 243-K (243-ZA for municipalities).

147.s: Who among the following constitutes a Finance Commission to review the financial position of the Panchayats?
147.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
147.x: The Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission (Art. 243-I) every five years to review the financial position of the Panchayats.

147.s: The Constitutional provision relating to the State Electoral Commission is:
147.x: The State Election Commission is provided for in Article 243-K; 243-I = State Finance Commission, 243-P = definitions in Part IXA.

147.s: Which part of the Constitution has the provisions for Panchayati Raj System?
147.x: Panchayati Raj is in Part IX 'The Panchayats' (Articles 243-243O); Part IXA is Municipalities, Part IV the DPSP.

147.s: The 73rd Amendment of the Indian Constitution deals with
147.x: The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 deals with rural Panchayats (Part IX); the 74th deals with Nagar Palikas.

147.s: When was the third-tier added to Indian Federal System?
147.x: The third tier (local government) was added by the 73rd and 74th Amendment Acts of 1992 (in force 1993), so 1992 is the keyed year.

147.s: Which one of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India deals with the issue of strengthening of the Panchayati Raj?
147.x: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to PRIs; the 42nd (1976), 44th (1978) and 86th (2002, education) deal with other matters.

147.s:
Assertion (A): The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act is a significant landmark in the evolution of grassroots democratic institutions in the country.
Reason (R): This Act has brought the Panchayath Raj institutions under the purview of justiciable part of the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
147.x: Laxmikanth: the Act gives PRIs constitutional status, bringing them under the justiciable part – so States must adopt the system – and it is a significant landmark in grassroots democracy; R explains A.

147.s:
Consider the following statements -
Assertion (A) : Political interference in the management of rural matters is now decreased at the local level.
Reason(R) : The Rural local governance institutions have been rejuvenated by the 73rd amendment to Constitution.
Select the correct answer using code given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
147.x: The 73rd Amendment rejuvenated rural local bodies (constitutional status, regular elections, SEC), which reduced political interference in their management; R explains A (UP Lower 1998 key).

147.s: The 73rd Amendment of the Constitution of India is related to –
o: Salaries and Privileges of Members of Parliament
147.x: The 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 inserted Part IX on Panchayats, so it relates to the Panchayati Raj system.

147.s: Panchayati Raj is organized as a unit of Self- Government under –
o: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution
147.x:
Most books and keys: 73rd Amendment. Strictly: the words 'units of self-government' come from Art. 40 (DPSP), to which the 73rd Amendment gave practical shape (Laxmikanth ch.39 p.102).
The book key is the 73rd Amendment, which constitutionalised Panchayats as units of self-government; the phrase 'organise village panchayats... as units of self-government' itself is Art. 40 (DPSP), which the Act put into effect.

147.s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about 73rd Amendment to the Indian Constitution?
1. It recognized Panchayats as institutions of selfgovernment.
2. It recognized urban local governments as institutions of self-government. Select the Correct answer using the codes given below:
Codes :
147.x: The 73rd Amendment recognised Panchayats (rural) as institutions of self-government; urban local governments came with the 74th.

147.s: The 73rd Amendment of Indian Constitution provides –
o: removal of administrative control over Panchayats
changing of laws regarding elections of Panchayats
making panchayat elections mandatory and equivalent
147.x: The Act made regular Panchayat elections mandatory under an SEC (243K) on a uniform pattern in all States; PRIs existed since 1959, and administrative control was not removed.

147.s: Which article of the Constitution provides for Audit of accounts of Panchayati Raj Institutions?
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
147.x: Art. 243J: the State Legislature may provide for maintenance and audit of Panchayat accounts; 243K is the SEC, 243L UTs, 243M exempted areas.

147.s: Article 243(J) of the Indian Constitution is related to.
o: Constitution of Finance commission to review
147.x: Article 243J deals with audit of accounts of Panchayats; the Finance Commission is 243I and elections 243K.

147.s: In context to Constitution of India which statement is correct?
147.x: 243A is the Gram Sabha, 243B the constitution of Panchayats and 243C their composition – only the 243C pair is right.

147.s: The Article 243-G of the Indian Constitution contains:
o: The financial resources of Panchayat Raj Bodies
The functions of the Nyaya Panchayats
The powers & functions of Village Panchayats
The powers & functions of chairpersons of Zilla Parishads and Mandal Parishads
147.x: Art. 243G covers the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats (with the Eleventh Schedule); finances are 243H and Nyaya Panchayats are not in Part IX.

147.s: Which of the following was constituted under the Panchayati Raj system?
147.x: The Gram Panchayat is the village-level body under Part IX; khap, caste and 'jan' panchayats are not constitutional bodies.

147.s: The major change that occurred in the Panchayati Raj System after the 73rd Constitutional Amendment is/ was
o: The States can decide the system
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
147.x: The 73rd Amendment made the structure uniform – three tiers in every State (middle tier optional below 20 lakh) – replacing the earlier State-by-State variety.

147.s: Provisions about the Panchayats were added to the Constitution by:
147.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
147.x: Part IX (The Panchayats) was added by the Constitution (73rd Amendment) Act, 1992; the 1980s numbers offered are unrelated.

147.s: Article ....... does not come under the 73rd Constitution (Amendment) Act.
147.x: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX, Articles 243 to 243-O; Article 243-P begins Part IXA (Municipalities, 74th Amendment), so 243(p) is not under the 73rd.

147.s: Which of the following articles is related to Panchayati Raj?
147.x: Part IX on Panchayats begins with Article 243 (243-243O); Arts. 147, 323 and 329 deal with other matters.

147.s: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment inserted the following sections in the Constitution?
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
147.x: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX, Articles 243 to 243-O.

147.s: Who is vested with the power of Social Audit of MNREGA programme?
147.src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
147.x: Section 17 of MGNREGA makes the Gram Sabha conduct regular social audits of all projects in the Gram Panchayat.

147.s: A Gram Sabha at the village level is:
o: An assembly of elected ward members only
An assembly of the Sarpanch and the Panchayat Secretary
An assembly of all adult landowners of the village
An assembly where all are registered voters
147.src: APPSC Group-II (Mains) Paper-II Social History & Constitutio
147.x: Art. 243(b): the Gram Sabha is the body of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village in the Panchayat area – an assembly of all registered voters.

147.s: Gram Panchayat Development Plan is an example for convergence of ____ Ministers.
147.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
147.x:
APPSC key: 19 Ministries. Mission Antyodaya / GPDP convergence is now put at 27 Ministries/Departments (Rajya Sabha answer, Dec 2024).
APPSC key: the GPDP is a convergence plan bringing together schemes of 19 Ministries/Departments (Mission Antyodaya now counts 27).

147.s: The vital part in preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans is
o: Collection of Data and Situation Analysis
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
147.x: GPDP guidelines begin with collection of data and situation analysis (Mission Antyodaya data, participatory appraisal), on which prioritisation and resource envelopes are built.

147.s: According to Article 243(A) of the Constitution of India inserted by 73rd Constitutional amendment act, the body comprising of all persons registered on the rolls of Gram Panchayat is:
147.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) 2
147.x: Art. 243(b)/243A: the body of all persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village in the Panchayat area is the Gram Sabha.

147.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate example of direct democracy?
o: Peoples Court by Civil Society Groups
Decisions taken by the Gram Sabha
147.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
147.x: In the Gram Sabha all registered voters of the village decide directly, so it is the best example of direct democracy; Panchayats are representative bodies and caste panchayats, polls or people's courts are not.

147.s: In terms of discharge of functions, the 73rd Constitutional Amendment equates Gram Sabha at village level to?
o: Treats Gram Sabha as an infallible body
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
147.x: Art. 243A gives the Gram Sabha such powers at the village level as the State Legislature provides – it is the village's deliberative assembly, as the Legislature is at the State level.

147.s: A body consisting of persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village within the area of panchayat is called as
147.x: Art. 243(b): the Gram Sabha is the body of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the Panchayat area – registered voters, not all adults, residents or Panchayat members.

147.s: A Gram Sabha at the village level is:
o: An assembly where all registered voters of the village are members
Anassembly where all residents are members
Anassembly where all elders are members
An assembly where government employees in the village are members
147.x: Art. 243(b): the Gram Sabha is the body of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the Panchayat area – registered voters, not all adults, residents or Panchayat members.

147.s: Gram Sabha Means
o: Persons of the territorial area of a Panchayat.
Person specified by the notification of the district authority.
Persons registered in electoral rolls to a Panchayat area at the village level.
147.x: Art. 243(b): the Gram Sabha is the body of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the Panchayat area – registered voters, not all adults, residents or Panchayat members.

147.s: Which of the following is an example of Direct Democracy? C
147.x: In the Gram Sabha all registered voters of the village decide directly, so it is the best example of direct democracy; Panchayats are representative bodies and caste panchayats, polls or people's courts are not.

147.s:
What is correct:
(i) In a Gram Panchayat there can be more than one village.
(ii) Meeting of Gram Sabha held in each village.
(iii) Meeting of Gram Sabha held in the headquarter of Gram Panchayat.
(iv) Meeting of Gram Panchayat held in each village.
(v) Meeting of Gram Panchayat held in the headquarter of Gram Panchayat.
147.x: A Gram Panchayat may cover more than one village (i); Gram Sabha meetings are held in each village (ii); Gram Panchayat meetings are held at its headquarters (v).

o: All adults with age of 18 years and above in the Panchayat area

All citizens residing in the Panchayat area
All persons allowed by the Gram Panchayat
147.x: Art. 243(b): the Gram Sabha is the body of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the Panchayat area – registered voters, not all adults, residents or Panchayat members.

147.s: For selection of beneficiary in PMAY (Gramin), who would conduct verification of housing deprivation data?
147.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
147.x: Under PMAY-G the SECC-based list of housing-deprived households is verified by the Gram Sabha before beneficiaries are finalised.

147.s:
Identify the plans that shall converge with Gram Panchayat Development Plan of a village?
a. Village Sanitation Plan
b. Labour Budget of MGNREGS
c. Village Nutrition Plan
d. Village Agriculture Plan
e. Village School Education Plan
f. Village water sustainability Plan
g. Village Livelihoods Plan
h. Village Natural Resource Management Plan
i. Village Disaster Management Plan
o: a, b, d and e only
b, f, g and h only

148.src: APPSC Group-II Services Screening Test (Notification No. 18/2016), held 26-02-2017 FN (Series A, GS/EP/200) · Q68

148.src: APPSC Group-II Services Screening Test (Notification No. 18/2016), held 26-02-2017 FN (Series A, GS/EP/200) · Q70

149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: East Godavari was the AP district the Government of India chose for the m-FMS (mobile fund management) pilot; this is a printed APPSC key the library does not cover.

149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: The AP key gives 1000 sq m as the minimum site area for a gated-community development; the AP layout rules found on the web did not state the figure.

149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201

149.s: Which of the following is the meaning of PRIA Soft?
o: The name of an accounting company
The name of a Non-Governmental Organisation
an accounting method developed by UNDP to be used by governments
Software used for accounts in of Panchayati Raj Institutions for better accountability and transparency
149.src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
149.x: PRIASoft is the Ministry of Panchayati Raj's accounting software for PRIs, for accountability and transparency – the most popular accounting application found in panchayats; it is not a company, NGO or UNDP method.

149.s: Which of the following are NOT the salient features of 'Model Accounting System' for Panchayat Raj Institutions?
o: Emphasizes on weekly upgradation of accounts
Classifies transactions on a three-tier structure
Is prescribed jointly by MoPR and the C&AG
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Weekly upgradation of accounts is not a feature of the Model Accounting System for PRIs, which is a cash-based, three-tier classified system prescribed by MoPR with the C&AG.

149.s: With regard to maintenance of accounts, Panchayati Raj Institutions have to follow?
o: Model Accounting frame work prepared by Central Government
There is conflicting opinion on this issue
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
149.x: PRIs follow the Model Accounting framework prepared by the Central Government (MoPR with the C&AG, 2009), not any software or statute of their choice.

149.s: The three-tier structure on which the financial transactions are classified as per Model Accounting System are
o: Functions (Major Head), Programmes (Minor Head) and Objects (Object Head)
Programmes (Major Head), Functions (Minor Head) and Objects (Object Head)
Objects (Major Head), Programmes (Minor Head) and Functions (Object Head)
Functions (Major Head), Objects (Minor Head) and Programmes (Object Head)
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: The Model Accounting System classifies PRI transactions in three tiers – function (major head), programme (minor head) and object (object head).

149.s: Panchayat Raj Institutions maintains accounts on?
o: Depends on choice of the PRI
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
149.x: Under the Model Accounting System PRI accounts are prepared on a cash basis (with features for a later move to accrual), not mercantile or hybrid.

149.s: The financial transactions of Panchayat Raj Institutions are classified on?
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
149.x: PRI transactions are classified on a three-tier structure: major head (function), minor head (programme) and object head.

149.s: The method adopted by Panchayati Raj Institutions for maintaining their accounts is
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201

The printed key is 'both single and double entry': States use either (Tamil Nadu village panchayats single entry, PRIASoft States double entry), so neither alone is universal.

149.s: What is the weightage given to the autonomy of the Panchayati Raj Institutions in the Devolution Index?
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
149.x: In the MoPR-TISS Devolution Index 'Autonomy of PRIs' carries 15 (finances 50, functionaries 15, functions 10).

149.s: The accounts of Panchayat Raj institutions are based on?
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
149.x:
Keys differ: this paper keys 'double entry'; another APPSC paper keys 'both single and double entry' for PRI accounts.
The printed key is double entry: PRIASoft, used for PRI accounts in AP, keeps double-entry books; the Model Accounting System itself is cash-based.

149.s: Surcharge Certificate is equal to
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
149.x: A surcharge certificate under the AP Panchayat Raj law is enforceable like a civil court decree, not a mere penalty.

149.s: Once the bills are approved for payment, the account section shall stamp all the bills as ____
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Once bills are approved for payment the accounts section stamps them 'Paid and cancelled' so they cannot be presented again.

149.s: Gram Panchayat's compulsory tax- Kolagarum is levied
o: Both on the village product sold by weight and on the village product sold by volume
Only on the village product sold by weight
Only on the village product sold by volume
Only on goods brought into the village from outside
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Kolagaram (katarusum) is levied on village produce sold in the village by weight, measurement or number (s.60(1)(b)).

149.s: Which is the register in Gram Panchayat office for the payment of salaries to the employees of Panchayat?
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Salaries of panchayat employees are paid through the Acquittance Register.

149.s: The fiscal year end for Gram Panchayat accounting system is:
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: The Gram Panchayat accounting year ends on 31 March, like the Government financial year.

149.s: Among following taxes levied by Gram Panchayat, which is optional in nature?
o: Vehicle tax and tax on Agricultural land for a specific purpose
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Under s.60(3) a Gram Panchayat may levy a vehicle tax and a tax on agricultural land for a specific purpose – these are optional; house tax and kolagaram are compulsory.

149.s: The first step after purchasing goods of durable nature in Gram Panchayat office is:
o: To enter in the demand register
To issue a receipt to the supplier
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Durable goods bought by the Gram Panchayat are first entered in the Stock Register.

149.s: The maximum period a Gram Panchayat is allowed to invest money not required for immediate use is:
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Money not needed for immediate use may be invested for at most three years (printed key).

149.s: The Third State Finance Commission of AP, recommended per capita grant to Zilla Parishad: Mandal Parishad: Gram Panchayat in the ratio of rupees?

149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev

149.s: The minimum percent of estimated receipts to be maintained as working balance in Gram Panchayat is:
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: A Gram Panchayat must keep a working balance of at least 5% of estimated receipts (printed key).

149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Betterment charges in such Gram Panchayats are Rs 50 per sq m (printed key).

149.s: What is the percentage of funds to be allocated to take up the welfare activities from Gram Panchayat Funds?
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
149.x: The printed key gives 10% of Gram Panchayat funds for welfare activities.

149.s: One of the Compulsory taxes to be collected by Gram Panchayat as a source of its revenue
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: House tax is a compulsory tax of every Gram Panchayat under s.60(1)(a), levied every year (s.61).

149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: A levy for a specific purpose over and above taxes on land is a cess (land cess under s.60(3)(iii)).

Fifty naya paise in the rupee
Twenty-Five naya paise in the rupee
Five naya paise in the rupee

149.s: The tax levied by the Gram Panchayat on the village produce sold in the village by weight, measurement or number is called ____
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: s.60(1)(b): kolagaram or katarusum is the tax on village produce sold in the village by weight, measurement or number.

149.s: Which of the following is not a source of funds for Gram Panchayat?

149.s: What is the percentage of earnest money deposit that a contractor has to deposit with Gram Panchayat while submitting the tenders for the development works in a Gram Panchayat area?

149.s: The application of PRIA Soft in Panchayat Raj Institutions is:

149.x: PRIASoft (Panchayati Raj Institutions Accounting Software) is the Ministry of Panchayati Raj's e-panchayat application for PRI accounts.

o: Grants are to be given without any conditions
Grants may be given for specific purpose only
Grants may not be directly transferred to Panchayats
Staff salaries shall not be counted under grants

149.x: AP identified 10 core subjects of the Eleventh Schedule for devolution to PRIs (the C&AG also speaks of '10 subjects assigned'); it has not devolved all 29.

149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: Per the APPSC key, Section 74 of the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 deals with the Gram Panchayat Fund.

149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201

o: A book of original entries only
A book of original entries and ledger accounts
A subsidiary book for credit transactions only

8 paise per rupee per annum on the annual rent of land

149.s: Own revenue generated by Panchayat Raj Institutions in Andhra Pradesh during 2014-15 is of the order of?

149.x: The key puts PRIs' own revenue in AP in 2014-15 at about Rs 300 crore, a small share of their receipts, since they depend mostly on transfers.

149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
149.x: Andhra Pradesh devolved functions of 10 line departments (agriculture, animal husbandry, drinking water, school education, health, social welfare, BC welfare, women and child welfare and others) to Panchayat Raj Institutions through orders of 2007-08, so 2008 is the nearest option.

149.s: A Panchayat Secretary in AP does not discharge functions related to?
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
149.x: School supervision is not a function of the AP Panchayat Secretary; village administration, community welfare and community development are.

149.s: The representative appointed by the Government in each panchayat is:

149.x: The Panchayat Secretary is the Government-appointed functionary (representative) in each gram panchayat; the Sarpanch is elected.

149.s: Panchayat Secretaries work under the administrative control of
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I

149.s: The District level Administrative Authority of the Gram Panchayat
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: The district-level administrative authority over gram panchayats is the Collector (Panchayat Raj) – printed key.

149.s: All officers and other employees of the Gram Panchayat shall be ____ to the gram panchayat.
149.src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
149.x: s.36(5): all officers and other employees of the gram panchayat shall be subordinate to the gram panchayat.

149.s: Any order of the Panchayat Secretary granting, refusing, suspending or revoking a license or permission can be appealed to ____

149.x: s.128(1)(a): an appeal lies to the Gram Panchayat from any order of the executive authority (Panchayat Secretary) granting, refusing, suspending or revoking a licence or permission.

149.x: If a Gram Panchayat abuses its powers the State Government (through the administration) can dissolve it; a panchayat can be dissolved before its term, with fresh polls within six months.

149.s: Who plays a vital role in establishing the Joint Action Committees to look after the works taken up with the funds of Gram Panchayat/ Mandal Parishad or Zilla Parishad and resolve the disputes that arise between two or more Panchayats?

Who served last term as Ward member

149.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S

149.x: s.31: Gram Panchayat meetings are convened by the Panchayat Secretary, with the approval or on the direction of the Sarpanch.

149.s: Who is authenticated to calculate the house tax for a newly constructed building in the area of Gram Panchayat?

149.s: Who will administer the cremation or burial of destitute human beings and animals in the village?
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201

149.s: Who has the power to scrutinize the records of the Gram Panchayat?
149.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
149.x: The Sarpanch has the power to scrutinise the records of the Gram Panchayat (printed key).

149.s: Who is responsible to inform of the births which happen at hospital, nursing home, jail, choultry, rest house, etc., and the dead corpse or the babies thrown into open places to the Gram Panchayat?

126.s:

C. A highlight of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC) is the inclusion of a specific chapter aimed at returning assets to their rightful owners from whom they had been taken illicitly.

118.s: The Inter-State Council under Article 263 was actually set up in which year, and on whose recommendation?
o: 1969, on the recommendation of the Rajamannar Committee
1966, on the recommendation of the Administrative Reforms Commission
1990, on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission
2007, on the recommendation of the Punchhi Commission
118.x: The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 under Article 263 following the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation. The ARC (1966) and the Rajamannar Committee (1969) had earlier supported such a body, but it was not set up on their advice. The Punchhi Commission came later.
xs: The ISC was set up in **1990** on the **Sarkaria Commission's** recommendation — so option **(3)** is correct.
**ARC (1966-69)** and **Rajamannar Committee (1969)** had backed it earlier but it was not set up on their advice.
xa: Set up under **Art 263** (APPSC-G1 **2017** key).
Sarkaria's term was a permanent "**Inter-Governmental Council**".
It is **recommendatory**, deciding by **consensus**.
118.tq: ISC = 1990, Sarkaria, PM in the chair.

118.s: Under Article 165(3), the Advocate General of a State holds office during the pleasure of whom?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
xs: The **Advocate General** holds office during the **pleasure of the Governor** (**Article 165(3)**), with **no fixed** tenure.
xa: Remuneration is fixed by the **Governor**.
118.x: The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor (Article 165(3)), with no fixed tenure.

118.s: A State's Advocate General serves during the pleasure of which authority?
xs: The **Advocate General** holds office during the **pleasure of the Governor** (**Article 165(3)**).
118.x: The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor (Article 165(3)).

Panchayats' share of State taxes as recommended by the State Finance Commission is called?
xs: Shared taxes: Share of state taxes as per SFC
118.x: Shared taxes: Share of state taxes as per SFC

118.s: Who prescribes the qualifications of Finance Commission members?
xs: **FC qualifications** = **Parliament by law**; **Lokpal Selection Committee** chair = **Prime Minister**.
118.x: FC qualifications = Parliament by law; Lokpal Selection Committee chair = Prime Minister.

118.s: A statutory body is created by what?
xs: A **statutory body** is created by an **Act of Parliament**
118.x: A statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament

118.s: The National Human Rights Commission comes under which ministry?
xs: **NCM** — Minority Affairs, **NHRC** — Home Affairs, **NCW** — Women and Child Development are correct.
118.x: NCM — Minority Affairs, NHRC — Home Affairs, NCW — Women and Child Development are correct.

118.s: The NHRC was set up on which date?
What is the legal status of the NHRC?
xs: The NHRC is **statutory**, not constitutional.
118.x: The NHRC is statutory, not constitutional.

118.s: The National Development Council was created by what?
xs: Union Cabinet ministers became members **since 1967**; the NDC was created by **executive resolution** in **August 1952**.
118.x: Union Cabinet ministers became members since 1967; the NDC was created by executive resolution in August 1952.

118.s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that the National Development Council should be given constitutional status under Article 263 and renamed as the:
118.x: The Sarkaria Commission recommended constitutional status for the NDC under Article 263 and proposed the name National Economic and Development Council.
xs: The **Sarkaria Commission** proposed renaming the NDC the **"National Economic and Development Council"** with **constitutional status under Art. 263** — option **(4)**.
Art. **263** is the basis of the **Inter-State Council**.
xa: The **NDC** was created by executive resolution in **August 1952**.
Members: **PM**, all Union Cabinet ministers (since **1967**), all CMs, UT administrators.
The **Inter-State Council** was set up by **Presidential order** in **1990**.
118.tq: Match a commission recommendation with the precise proposed institutional name and Article.

118.s: The National Security Council of India is best described as:
o: A statutory body set up under an Act of Parliament in 1998
An extra-constitutional body set up by an executive order in 1998
A statutory body under the North Eastern Council Act, 1971
118.x: The National Security Council is an extra-constitutional body created by an executive order in 1998; it has neither constitutional nor statutory basis.
xs: The **National Security Council** is **extra-constitutional**, set up by an **executive order in 1998** — option **(3)**.
It has no constitutional (Art. **263** is the Inter-State Council) or statutory basis.
xa: **Planning Commission (1950)** and **NDC (1952)** were also created by executive resolution.
**NEC** is statutory under the **NEC Act 1971**.
**Inter-State Council:** Presidential order, **1990**.
118.tq: NSC 1998: born of an executive order, not law.

118.s: A non-judicial body empowered under a statute to apply law, summon persons and impose sanctions is called?
xs: A **quasi-judicial** body is a **non-judicial** body that can **interpret and apply law**, **examine**, **summon** and **impose sanctions** under a statute
118.x: A quasi-judicial body is a non-judicial body that can interpret and apply law, examine, summon and impose sanctions under a statute

118.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally regarded as a quasi-judicial body in the context described?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
118.x: NITI Aayog is an advisory body and is not quasi-judicial. NHRC, SEBI and CIC are examples of bodies having quasi-judicial features.
xs: **NITI Aayog** is an **advisory** body, NOT quasi-judicial — option **(1)**.
**SEBI**, **CIC** and **NHRC** are listed examples of quasi-judicial bodies.
xa: Definition: a **non-judicial** body that can interpret and apply law, **summon**, and impose sanctions.
The **Law Commission** is also advisory and **not quasi-judicial**.
NITI Aayog is the **odd one out** among NCBC, CAG, Finance Commission (**APPSC-GS 2025**).
118.tq: Remove the advisory institution from the group of bodies that apply law or adjudicate statutory matters.

118.s: Which of the following bodies has civil court powers such as summoning witnesses and requisitioning records?
118.x: The NCBC has powers of a civil court, including summoning witnesses and requisitioning records, particularly after it received constitutional status in 2018.
xs: The **NCBC** has **civil court powers** (summon witnesses, requisition records) since **2018** — option **(3)**.
The **NDC**, **Law Commission** and **NITI Aayog** are executive/advisory and lack such powers.
xa: Others with civil court powers: **NHRC**, **NCM**, **NCSC and NCST**, **NCW**, **CIC** (RTI Act).
NCBC got Art. **338B** via the **102nd Amendment (2018)**.
Quasi-judicial examples: **SEBI**, **Mental Health Review Commission**.
118.tq: Use the ‘civil court powers’ clue to distinguish commissions from advisory bodies.

118.s: State Commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes are established under what?

Zonal Councils were created under which law?

118.x: Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first (ex officio) Chairman of the Planning Commission; Arvind Panagariya the first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog.

118.x: It is provided for under Article 263 and was set up by Presidential order.

118.s: Who headed the First Official Language Commission?
xs: The **First Official Language Commission** was set up in **1955**, headed by **B.G. Kher**.
118.x: The First Official Language Commission was set up in 1955, headed by B.G. Kher.

118.s: Which of these institutions was established first?
xs: **Planning Commission** (**1950**) → **National Development Council** (**1952**) → **Inter-State Council** (**1990**) → **NITI Aayog** (**2015**).
xa: Planning Commission: **Cabinet Resolution** of **15 March 1950**; NDC: **Executive Order** of **6 August 1952**.
The **Advisory Planning Board** (**1946**, K.C. Neogi) preceded the Planning Commission.
118.x: Planning Commission (1950) → National Development Council (1952) → Inter-State Council (1990) → NITI Aayog (2015).

118.s: Which of the following is an extra-constitutional or non-statutory body?
118.x: The Law Commission is set up from time to time by executive order, so it is extra-constitutional. The SC Commission, Finance Commission and State Election Commission are constitutional.
xs: The **Law Commission of India** is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body — option **(1)**.
It is constituted **periodically** by **executive order** — a Department of Legal Affairs notification **every 3 years**.
The others are **constitutional**: **NCSC** (**Art. 338**), **Finance Commission** (**Art. 280**), **State Election Commission** (**243-K** and **243-ZA**).
xa: The Law Commission is **advisory**, **not quasi-judicial**, and reports to the **Ministry of Law and Justice**.
The **23rd Law Commission** runs **1 Sep 2024 - 31 Aug 2027**.
⚠ APPSC-G1 2024 keyed "All incorrect" for statements calling it a quasi-judicial body advising the President.
First Law Commission of independent India: **M.C. Setalvad**, **1955**.
118.tq: Classify a body by where its power comes from: Constitution, statute or order.

118.s: The Law Commission of India is constituted periodically by what?
xs: **Law Commission** → constituted periodically by **executive order**; **NDC** → **Executive Order** of **6 August 1952**.
118.x: Law Commission → constituted periodically by executive order; NDC → Executive Order of 6 August 1952.

118.s: Which Article deals with laying the Finance Commission's recommendations before Parliament?
xs: Under **Article 281**, the report is **submitted** to the **President**, who causes it to be **laid before both Houses**.
118.x: Under Article 281, the report is submitted to the President, who causes it to be laid before both Houses.

118.s: Zonal Councils are what kind of bodies?
xs: **Zonal Councils** are **statutory** bodies under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**.
118.x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

118.s: The Inter-State Council has its basis in which Article?
xs: The **Inter-State Council** rests on **Article 263** — a **constitutional** basis — which is why the two are distinct.
118.x: The Inter-State Council rests on Article 263 — a constitutional basis — which is why the two are distinct.

118.s: Which of these constitutional changes came last?
o: Multi-member NCSC and NCST under Article 338

xs: The **qualifications** of members are determined by **Parliament** by **law**.
118.x: The qualifications of members are determined by Parliament by law.

118.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes got its Article through which amendment?
xs: **89th Amendment, 2003**.
118.x: 89th Amendment, 2003.

118.x: Executive / non-statutory body: Resolution-based, advisory (NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC, Law Commission)

xs: **JSPSC** → **each Governor concerned**; **each State Legislature**. **NCSC/NCST/NCBC** → President; Parliament.

**Finance Commission** → President; Parliament with an explanatory memorandum (Art. **281**). **SPSC** → Governor; State Legislature.
118.x: JSPSC → each Governor concerned; each State Legislature. NCSC/NCST/NCBC → President; Parliament.

xs: The **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities** (Art.

In the order of precedence, which of the following groups is placed at rank 9A?
o: Chairperson of UPSC, Chief Election Commissioner and Comptroller and Auditor General
Chairpersons of NCM, NCSC and NCST
Chairperson of the Finance Commission, Attorney General and Cabinet Secretary
Chairpersons of the State Election Commission and State Finance Commission
118.x: The Chairperson of the UPSC, the Chief Election Commissioner and the CAG are placed at rank 9A in the order of precedence. The Chairpersons of NCM, NCSC and NCST are placed at rank 17.
xs: **UPSC Chairperson**, **Chief Election Commissioner** and **CAG** are at rank **9A** — option **(1)**.
The chairpersons of **NCM, NCSC and NCST** are at rank **17**, so option 2 is wrong.
xa: UPSC (Art. **315**), Election Commission (Art. **324**) and CAG (Art. **148**) are **constitutional** bodies.

118.s: Under Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, the Central Bureau of Investigation generally requires which of the following?

Consent of the Supreme Court in every case
Approval of the Election Commission of India
118.x: Section 6 of the DSPE Act requires the consent of the concerned State Government for exercising CBI powers in that State. Several States have withdrawn general consent.

2.s: "Culture is the part created by man in the environment". Who said this ?
2.x: 'Culture is the man-made part of the environment' is M.J. Herskovits's definition (Man and His Works, 1948). Tylor defined culture as a 'complex whole' of knowledge, belief, art, morals, law and custom, and Malinowski as inherited artefacts, goods and ideas, so 'None of the above'.

2.s: Who first mentioned the concept of "social evolution" ?
2.x: Herbert Spencer was among the first to study society from an evolutionary point of view; his Social Statics (1851) already framed social evolution, and he coined 'survival of the fittest'. Comte gave the law of three stages, Lester Ward 'telesis' (printed key: Lester F. Ward).

2.s: Who said "Society is a fabric of social relations"?
2.x: MacIver and Page called society 'a web (fabric) of social relationships'. Weber is linked with social action, Veblen with the leisure class and Marx with class struggle.

2.s: "Society is like a weaving work of social relations." With whom of the following is this comment associated?
2.x: 'Society is a web of social relationships' is MacIver's definition (MacIver and Page, Society); it is not from Marx, Durkheim or Weber.

2.s: Who proposed the concept of "Social capillary" ?
2.x: 'Social capillarity' was coined by the French demographer Arsène Dumont (Dépopulation et Civilisation, 1890): the pursuit of upward mobility makes families limit births, like liquid rising in a capillary tube. Louis Dumont (Homo Hierarchicus) is the caste scholar, a trap (printed key: Louis Dumont).

2.s: What kind of authority does the tribal leader exercise ?
2.x: A tribal chief's authority rests on custom and tradition, so it is Weber's traditional authority, not rational-legal or magical power.

2.s: Which of the following is included in Weber's typology of action ?
o: Rational action with respect to purpose, rational action with respect to values, emotional action, conventional action
Conventional Action, Populist Action, Rational Action
2.x: Weber's four types of social action are instrumentally (goal) rational, value-rational, affective (emotional) and traditional (conventional).

2.s: According to Karl Marx, class membership is based on what ?
2.x: For Marx, class is fixed by one's position in the relations of production (owners vs non-owners of the means of production), not by authority or prestige (Weber).

2.s: Who among the following termed sociology as "social physics" ?
2.x: Auguste Comte first called the new science 'social physics' and later renamed it 'sociology' (1838), partly because Quetelet had used 'social physics' for statistics.

2.s: Who included India in the Asiatic Mode of Production?
2.x: Karl Marx placed India in the 'Asiatic mode of production' (writings on India 1853-58): village communities without private landed property under a despotic state. Weber wrote The Religion of India (printed key: Max Weber).

2.s: What is the habit of a person occupying a position of traditional authority based on a belief in holiness and obedience?
2.x: Authority resting on belief in the sanctity of age-old custom and obedience to its holder is Weber's traditional authority.

2.s: Who is the author of the book 'Sociology of Economic Life'?
2.x: The Sociology of Economic Life (1963) is by Neil J. Smelser.

2.s: Who described Sociology as the encyclopedic science of society?
2.x: Comte (and Spencer) saw sociology as a synthetic, encyclopaedic science of society, the queen of the sciences; Sorokin and MacIver held the specialist (formal) view.

2.s: It is said that "Religion is an intoxicant of people". Who said?
